chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who brings me silver coins (dirhams), so I buy them from him with gold coins (dinars), while I occupy myself with determining their weight, checking their quality, and the best of what is between me and him regarding them. Then I give him the gold coins and say to him: 'There is no sale between me and you, and I have annulled what was between me and you of the sale, and your silver is a loan with me, and my gold is a loan with you,' until tomorrow comes and I conclude the transaction with him. He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

Ishaq said: And I asked him about a man who sells me silver for gold, and I weigh from him and weigh for him until I finish, so there is no action between me and him except that in his silver there is excess (defect/impurity) and counterfeit and what is not permissible. So he says: 'Check it and return the excess.' He said: 'There is no harm in it, but that should not be delayed more than a day or two, for it is merely exchange (currency exchange).'
I said: 'If I find in his silver an excess equal to the amount of the defect in it?' He said: 'This is precaution, this is more preferable to me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying the finalization of a silver-for-gold currency exchange to check for quality?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of deferring the finalization of a gold-for-silver exchange by treating the initial transfer as a loan (qard) for up to two days, a ruling that accommodates the practical need for weighing and verifying purity (nuflah) without falling into riba. This permissibility is rooted in the principle that such transactions remain within the bounds of *sarf* (currency exchange), provided the delay is brief and any excess found is returned as a precaution (*ihtiyat*). This hadith highlights the Shia juristic flexibility in commercial transactions, distinguishing between the immediate exchange of value and the procedural delay required for quality assurance.
